title: Lists
short_description: Store and modify collections of data.
bro_quote: Lists are your data containers—learn to organize, manipulate, and iterate through your data.

subtopics.name: Creating Lists
subtopics.explanation:
• 📋 A list is a collection that holds multiple items in order.
  • 🔢 Use square brackets [] to create a list.
  • 🎯 Items are separated by commas. Example: [1, 2, 3]
  • ✅ Lists can hold any data type: numbers, strings, booleans, even other lists.
  • 🔄 Lists are mutable — you can change, add, or remove items.

subtopics.name: Indexing and Accessing Items
subtopics.explanation:
• 💺 Items are numbered starting from 0 (first item is at index 0).
  • 🔙 Use negative indices to count from the end: -1 is last, -2 is second to last.
  • 🎯 Use square brackets to access: list[index]
  • ⚠️ Index out of range causes an error. Check list length first.

snippets.code:
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "orange"]
print(fruits[0])    # apple
print(fruits[2])    # orange
print(fruits[-1])   # orange (last item)

subtopics.name: Modifying Lists
subtopics.explanation:
• ✏️ Change an item using list[index] = new_value
  • ➕ .append() adds an item to the END.
  • 📍 .insert(index, value) adds at a specific position.
  • ❌ .remove(value) deletes the first matching item.
  • 🔤 .pop(index) removes and returns an item (default: last item).

subtopics.name: List Methods
subtopics.explanation:
• 📊 .sort() arranges items in order (modifies original list).
  • 🔄 .reverse() flips the order (modifies original list).
  • 📏 len() returns how many items are in the list.
  • 🔍 .count(value) counts how many times a value appears.
  • 📍 .index(value) returns the position of a value.
  • 🧹 .clear() removes all items.

subtopics.name: Slicing Lists
subtopics.explanation:
• ✂️ Use list[start:end] to get a portion of the list.
  • 📌 Start is included, end is excluded. Example: [0:2] gets items at index 0 and 1.
  • 🚀 Omit start or end to slice from beginning or to the end.
  • 📊 Use step to skip items: list[start:end:step]

subtopics.name: List Iteration and Comprehension
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔁 Loop through lists with for item in list
  • 🔢 Use for i in range(len(list)) when you need the index.
  • 💡 List comprehensions create new lists concisely.
  • 🎯 [expression for item in list] applies operation to each item.

snippets.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
squares = [x**2 for x in numbers]
print(squares)  # [1, 4, 9, 16, 25]

questions: 1. Create a list containing four different types of fruit. (Creating list)
2. Print the third item in your list using its index number. (Accessing)
3. Change the value of the second item in your list to something else. (Modifying)
4. Add a completely new item to the very end of your list. (Appending)
5. Insert a new item exactly at the beginning (index 0) of the list. (Inserting)
6. Remove a specific value (like 'apple') from your list. (Removing)
7. Use the .pop() method to remove and print the last item. (Popping)
8. Sort a list of numbers from lowest to highest. (Sorting)
9. Reverse the order of all items currently in your list. (Reversing)
10. Use len() to figure out exactly how many items your list currently holds. (List length)
